neighbours.label: infectious-disease outbreak vocabulary: 'pandemic', 'epidemic', 'public health emergency', 'COVID', 'microcephaly' in an outbreak context
fire: The mayor announced a public health emergency after the cholera cases doubled.
Shops were shuttered for months during the coronavirus pandemic.
A flu epidemic swept the barracks in the autumn of 1918.
Mothers infected with Zika gave birth to babies with microcephaly.
The province declared a public health emergency as the virus spread.
Airlines cut flights when the COVID-19 pandemic began.
The polio epidemic left thousands of children paralysed.
Officials feared a new H1N1 pandemic would overwhelm the wards.
quiet: The mayor announced a hiring freeze after the budget gap doubled.
Shops were shuttered for months during the road works.
A fire swept the barracks in the autumn of 1918.
Mothers with diabetes gave birth to babies with higher birth weight.
The province declared a holiday as the festival began.
Airlines cut flights when the fuel price rose.
The car accident left three children with broken legs.
Officials feared the new hospital wing would open late.

notes: Weak pole (max 8.3). Probes: 0.23-0.34 on pandemic / epidemic / public health emergency / microcephaly, 0.03 on a budget emergency or a snowstorm. ' acute' fired 0.27 with or without infection, so it is kept out of the test; the - pole fires on transmission routes (contact, day care, travel).
